why: The inserted principle forbidding cuts that separate heads from required complements caused the model to avoid splitting prepositional/complement spans and instead shift cuts earlier (often between verbs/subjects and following prepositions), which helps cohesion for long pieces but produced many harmful single-word or very-short pieces — hurting the ≤3 and ≤7 bins and yielding slightly more worse (199) than better (167) pairs.
lesson: A later revision should respect that banning head–complement splits can force cuts into short-span head–dependent links (creating isolated words or subject–verb splits); avoid changes that improve long-span cohesion while degrading small-bin coherence.
